name: Tetanus and adult diphtheria vaccine (Td) in pregnancy
protects_against: Tetanus and diphtheria, in the mother and the newborn

indications.reason: India's national schedule gives Td to pregnant women: Td-1 early in pregnancy and Td-2 four weeks later, or a single booster if you were vaccinated in a pregnancy within the last 3 years.
indications.section: For pregnant women: TT/Td-1, TT/Td-2, TT/Td booster

series.note: One dose (a booster) is enough if you received Td or TT doses in a pregnancy within the last 3 years.

safety_note: The national schedule document does not list contraindications. Tell the health worker about any serious reaction to a previous vaccine or any severe allergy.

content.disease: Tetanus causes painful stiffening of the muscles. Diphtheria can lead to difficulty breathing, heart failure, paralysis or death.
content.why: Vaccinating during pregnancy protects the mother and the newborn from tetanus and diphtheria.
content.who: Pregnant women, as part of routine antenatal care.
content.doses_text: Td-1 early in pregnancy, Td-2 four weeks after Td-1. Or one booster dose if you were vaccinated in a pregnancy within the last 3 years.
content.catch_up: Td is given free at government health facilities as part of the Universal Immunization Programme. Ask at your antenatal visit.
common_reactions: Pain, redness or swelling where the shot was given
serious_reactions: People sometimes faint after medical procedures, including vaccination.
A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
